name: Dax Wave and Groom

lead: Dax Wave and Groom is a thick hair dress sold under the Dax brand, a company that makes pomades, waxes, creams and shampoos. Retail listings describe it as a product to bring out natural wave patterns in hair.
It is used with a brush on short, textured hair to hold ripples flat and add sheen, so waves look more defined. As a styling product it works while applied, and no research examines it.

paras: Users apply a small amount to short hair, then brush the pattern in and often cover it with a durag, which are the standard steps of the wave routine. Because the formula is heavy, they report washing with clarifying shampoo to remove it.

Petrolatum- and lanolin-based pomades can build up on scalp and hair, and users report that they are difficult to wash out. People with lanolin sensitivity may react, and heavy products can clog pores along the hairline.

chain: Thick pomade applied to short hair
Brushing lays curls in a ripple pattern
angle.text: The pomade coats and weighs the hair so brushed waves stay flat and glossy. The effect lasts until washed out.

lead: Dax Wave and Groom is a heavy pomade made by Dax. Retail listings describe it as a thick hair dress with a petroleum-jelly and lanolin base.

The look it serves is waves, a style in which curly or kinky hair is brushed into a ripple pattern. Wikipedia describes the style as using a short-cropped top, frequent brushing, silky durags and pomade or moisturiser to keep hair in place; the style became popular among African-American men in the early twentieth century [1]. Pomade overall peaked from the 1920s to 1950s and returned in the 2010s [2].
infobox: Petrolatum, mineral oil, lanolin (per retail listings)

paras: Traditional oil-based pomades come in heavy, medium and light holds, and light versions called brilliantine are shinier; water-based pomades wash out more easily [2]. Dax Wave and Groom belongs to the heavy petroleum-based type, which retailers describe as a thick dress for bringing out wave patterns.
Wave routines combine brushing, a durag and a pomade or moisturiser; brushing trains curls to lie flat and the durag holds the pattern and keeps hair moisturised [1].
Users consistently report that the pomade is hard to wash out, with some recommending brand shampoos or repeated washing [2].
